clinical_rationale: Systolic BP >= 180 mmHg represents hypertensive urgency/crisis with immediate risk of cerebrovascular accident or acute heart failure.
Diastolic pressure >= 110 mmHg causes severe end-organ vascular stress.
Pulse oximetry SpO2 <= 90% indicates respiratory compromise, acute pulmonary edema, or severe asthma exacerbation.
Resting heart rate >= 115 bpm may indicate decompensation, arrhythmia, sepsis, or severe pain.
Blood glucose >= 250 mg/dL increases hyperosmolar and ketoacidosis risk.
Pain score >= 8/10 signals acute clinical decompensation or uncontrolled condition.
Adherence <= 70% precipitates disease recurrence, rebound hypertension, or loss of glycemic control.
